description: FIRST TWISTED-EXTRUDE GOLDEN (helical-gear gap #1, docs/design/twisted-extrude.md). A 20 x 20 mm square centred on the XY origin with an OFF-AXIS r3 hole at (4, 0), extruded 30 mm along +Z with twist_angle_deg = 30 about the default axis (the sketch origin): every slice is the profile turned by 1 deg per mm, so each point traces a true helix and the lateral faces are screw-swept surfaces (BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipeShell along a straight spine, auxiliary helix; B-spline fits at 1e-7 mm). Locks: the twisted sweep and its tolerance, the holed-profile path (outer and hole swept separately, hole cut out), the RIGHT-HAND-about-travel sign convention, and (via the parametrized gates) in-process + interpreter-restart byte determinism and the STEP round trip. The hole is off-axis on purpose: a centred profile is symmetric under the twist, so a mirrored helix would pass every mass property; this one puts the handedness in centroid.y.
derivation: Every expectation is ANALYTIC, hand-derived below; the measured deviations are recorded beside each one (2026-09-24, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9, pipe-shell fit 1e-7 mm).

Notation: a = 10 (square half-width), h = 30, hole r = 3 at eccentricity e = 4, total twist T = 30 deg = pi/6, twist rate k = T/h = pi/180 rad/mm. The slice at height z is the z = 0 profile rotated by k*z about the Z axis (counter-clockwise seen from +Z, because a positive twist is right-handed about the direction of travel and that direction is +Z).

volume: every slice is congruent to the profile, so by Cavalieri V = A*h EXACTLY for any twist, A = 4a^2 - pi r^2 = 400 - 9 pi = 371.72566611769184. V = 11151.769983530756 mm^3. Measured deviation +2.74e-7 mm^3 (2.5e-11 relative): the B-spline fit of the helicoidal flanks.

surface_area = outer flanks + hole tube + 2 caps. A surface swept by the screw motion P(s,z) = R(kz) p(s) + z e_z has |dP/ds x dP/dz| = sqrt(1 + k^2 (p . t)^2) for a unit-speed profile curve p(s) with unit tangent t, independent of z. (i) Each square side: p . t = s runs over [-a, a], so a side contributes h * [a sqrt(1 + k^2 a^2) + asinh(k a)/k]; four sides = 2412.1296186122354. (ii) The hole, p = (e + r cos f, r sin f), t = (-sin f, cos f), so p . t = -e sin f and the tube is h r * integral_0^2pi sqrt(1 + k^2 e^2 sin^2 f) df (a complete elliptic integral; evaluated by the trapezoid rule, exponentially convergent for a smooth periodic integrand: 566.1750776220302 at 20000 and 566.1750776220307 at 40000 nodes) - 0.69 mm^2 more than the straight r3 cylinder's 565.4866776461628, which is the twist made visible. (iii) Caps 2A = 743.4513322353837. Total 3721.756028469649 mm^2. Measured deviation +4.31e-8 mm^2 (fixed-order area integration, as in every golden).

centroid: the slice centroid at z = 0 is c0 = (-(pi r^2) e / A, 0) = (-0.30424946630783595, 0) (the hole removes material right of the axis). Slice z has centroid R(kz) c0, so the solid's is c0 times the mean rotation: x = c0 sin(T)/T = -0.2905368389757789, y = c0 (1 - cos T)/T = -0.07784911137505107, z = h/2 = 15. y < 0 IS THE HANDEDNESS: a left-hand (or mirrored) twist gives +0.0778. Measured deviation <= 5.7e-12 mm.

bounding_box: the hole never reaches the outline (its farthest point is 7 mm from the axis, inside the 10 mm inscribed circle), so the extent is the square's. A square of half-width a turned by t in [0, 45 deg] reaches a(cos t + sin t), increasing in t, so over t in [0, 30 deg] the widest slice is the TOP one: x and y both span +-a(cos 30 + sin 30) = +-13.660254037844386; z spans [0, 30]. Measured: every bound padded outward by 1.0e-7, the optimal-AABB modelling-tolerance padding the loft goldens document.

topology, hand-derived: 4 flank faces (one per square side) + 1 hole tube + 2 planar caps = 7 faces; edges = 4 bottom + 4 top + 4 helical corner edges + 2 hole circles + 1 tube seam = 15; 1 closed shell. Same counts as the untwisted holed prism - a twist changes the surfaces, never the topology. EDGE GEOMETRY (since the review of d823af9): the 8 cap sides are exact LINES and the 2 hole rims exact CIRCLES - the pipe shell rebuilds them as B-spline fits and the kernel restores their analytic curves (twist._restore_cap_edges); only the 5 helical edges are B-splines. test_twisted_extrude asserts that census.

MESH counts are recorded, not derived, as in every golden: an exact-match determinism/regression tripwire on the 0.1 mm linear-deflection tessellation of the B-spline flanks. Re-recorded 3751/6874 -> 3557/6554 when the cap edges became analytic lines and circles again (a line edge is discretised with fewer nodes than its B-spline fit); the topology was unchanged and the mass properties moved by less than 1e-8 (volume residual +2.741e-7 before and after, area 6e-9, STEP round-trip drift 4e-9).
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill). The largest measured deviation from the analytic values is the VOLUME, +2.74e-7 mm^3 - the pipe-shell B-spline fit of the screw-swept flanks, which saturates at the 1e-7 mm fit tolerance the kernel uses (1e-8 gives the identical body; 1e-5 and 1e-6 give +2.70e-4, which is why the kernel does not use OCCT's 1e-4 default). Next is the AABB's modelling-tolerance padding, 1.0e-7 on all six bounds, then the area (4.3e-8) and the centroid (<= 5.7e-12). 2e-6 is 7.3x the worst case and 20x the AABB padding, while being ~1e-10 relative on the volume: a fit that loosened to the OCCT default (2.7e-4) fails this golden by two orders of magnitude, and so does ANY handedness error (centroid.y moves by 0.156 mm). Loosening it requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
